title: OpenAI Accuses Apple of Blocking Suppliers, Talent Raids
summary: OpenAI files counterclaims against Apple, alleging the iPhone maker pressured suppliers to avoid working with the AI company and used restrictive employment
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI filed counterclaims against Apple on November 27, 2026, alleging the iPhone maker pressured suppliers to shun OpenAI projects and block talent.
- The AI company claims Apple forces suppliers to identify workers with Apple experience and exclude them from OpenAI work, raising costs.
- OpenAI is developing hardware products with Jony Ive, including a rumored smart speaker, putting it in direct competition with Apple devices.


OpenAI has escalated its legal fight with Apple Inc., filing counterclaims that accuse the iPhone maker of deliberately undermining the AI company's hardware ambitions. Filed on November 27, 2026 in federal court in San Jose, California, the counterclaims allege Apple pressured suppliers to avoid working with OpenAI and used restrictive employment agreements to prevent engineers from joining the ChatGPT maker.


## Official Filing Date and Context


Officially launched on November 27, 2026, OpenAI's counterclaims transform Apple's original July lawsuit into a two-way intellectual property battle. The escalation comes as OpenAI prepares to enter the consumer hardware market with former Apple design chief Jony Ive, developing products that include a rumored doughnut-shaped smart speaker. Apple had initially sued OpenAI and Tang Tan, the AI company's chief hardware officer, alleging orchestrated theft of trade secrets through job candidates and former Apple employees.


## Supplier Interference Allegations


According to the filing, Apple has systematically pressured industry suppliers to identify their OpenAI projects and disclose names, locations, and assignments of workers with Apple experience. OpenAI alleges that Apple then seeks to exclude workers with OpenAI experience from future Apple work, effectively discouraging suppliers from committing resources to OpenAI projects.


One specialist finishing services supplier reportedly moved its OpenAI manufacturing work to the night shift to avoid overlapping with Apple projects, increasing costs for the AI company. OpenAI claims suppliers have expressed fear of losing Apple business, with some rescheduling meetings to avoid being seen working with OpenAI personnel. Other suppliers told OpenAI they must be cautious about devoting staff, production resources, or managerial attention to the AI company's projects.


## Employment Agreement Restrictions


OpenAI's counterclaims challenge Apple's employment agreements, particularly provisions that bar former Apple employees from soliciting or recruiting Apple workers for one year. The AI company argues that Apple's intellectual property agreements use an overly broad definition of confidential information, covering all nonpublic information employees learn during their tenure regardless of whether it qualifies as a trade secret.


These restrictions, OpenAI contends, unfairly limit former employees' professional skills and put them at risk of litigation. The filing states that even meritless lawsuits create expensive, invasive processes that may involve Apple examining former employees' personal devices and accounts. This threat gives Apple's employment provisions enforcement power beyond their legal validity.


## Trade Secrets Counteraccusations


OpenAI has turned Apple's original allegations around, accusing the iPhone maker of stealing the AI company's trade secrets. A former OpenAI employee who returned to Apple allegedly sent over one hundred highly confidential files about at least one unreleased OpenAI device to personal accounts. These files included images of unreleased hardware, engineering and manufacturing data, and supplier information.


Apple has responded by stating it maintains policies preventing use of confidential information from former employers, found no evidence substantiating OpenAI's claims, and believes the AI company is attempting to distract from significant evidence that OpenAI employees took Apple product information. The iPhone maker's lawsuit specifically names former iPhone engineer Chang Liu, who joined OpenAI in January 2026 and allegedly accessed confidential hardware files after discovering an authentication bug.


## What This Means


The legal battle between OpenAI and Apple represents a critical inflection point as AI companies increasingly compete in hardware markets traditionally dominated by consumer electronics giants. OpenAI's allegations suggest Apple may be leveraging its market power over suppliers and talent to protect its hardware business from AI-native competitors. With OpenAI voluntarily agreeing in October not to use trade secrets Apple claims were stolen, the case now hinges on whether Apple's supplier and employment practices constitute unlawful market exclusion. The outcome could set precedents for how established tech companies can defend their markets against AI upstarts entering hardware spaces.
